title: Swim Pace Fade Across Intervals
dataSources: Bar-velocity reps (`vbt:rep`), sprint reps (`sprint:rep`), serve attempts (`serve:attempt`), pickleball rallies (`pickleball:rally`), swim sets (`swim:set`), archery ends (`archery:end`), balance trials (`balance:trial`), and batting reps (`batting:rep`).
app: Sports and skill telemetry from VBT devices, sprint timers, serve trackers, swim logs, archery apps, balance trainers, and batting sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=swim:set
| stats earliest(pace_sec_100m) as first_pace_sec_100m latest(pace_sec_100m) as last_pace_sec_100m by workout_id stroke
| eval fade_sec=round(last_pace_sec_100m-first_pace_sec_100m,1)
| sort - fade_sec
description: Measures how much pace slows from the first to the last interval in a swim set.
value: Pace fade is a clean signal of conditioning and pacing strategy because it captures how a set finishes, not just how it starts.
implementation: Record interval pace in chronological order for each workout and stroke from your swim watch or logbook.
visualization: Table of first pace, last pace, and fade by workout and stroke.
grandmaExplanation: It maps how much your swim pace drops off by the end of a set.
